2610.07184.title: Learning Scientific Exploration from Human Research Decision Trajectories
2610.07184.paper_summary: A key challenge in building AI systems for scientific research is enabling $\textit{scientific exploration}$: the systematic process of investigating unknown phenomena or ideas to gain new knowledge through sequences of research decisions and actions. Yet this process is largely missing from existing scientific corpora; for example, research papers primarily record final outcomes rather than the trajectories that produced them. In this work, we introduce $\textbf{ResearchTrails}$, a dataset of $\textbf{human research trajectories constructed from Git repositories}$, where $\textbf{commit histories}$ serve as proxies for research exploration. We develop an automated and scalable pipeline that extracts structured research trajectories from repository commits, capturing successive changes to methods, experiments, and ablations. We characterize the resulting dataset and show that these trajectories contain meaningful signals about intermediate research decisions beyond what final papers reveal. We further demonstrate utilities of ResearchTrails in multiple use cases, including retrieving human research experience as external skills at test time and training models on research trajectories to improve generalization to new research decisions. Our results suggest a path toward AI systems that learn not only from the products of science, but from the evolving process of discovery itself.
2610.07184.paper_summary_zh: 一個在為科學研究構建AI系統時面臨的主要挑戰是實現$\textit{科學探索}$：這是一個系統性調查未知現象或想法的過程，通過一系列研究決策和行動來獲得新知識。然而，這一過程在現有的科學語料庫中大多缺失；例如，研究論文主要記錄最終結果，而不是產生這些結果的過程。在這項工作中，我們介紹了$\textbf{ResearchTrails}$，這是一個由$\textbf{從Git庫構建的人類研究軌跡}$組成的數據集，其中$\textbf{提交歷史}$作為研究探索的代理。我們開發了一個自動化且可擴展的管道，從庫提交中提取結構化的研究軌跡，捕捉方法、實驗和消融的連續變化。我們對生成的數據集進行了特徵描述，並顯示這些軌跡包含關於中間研究決策的有意義信號，超越了最終論文所揭示的內容。我們進一步展示了ResearchTrails在多個用例中的實用性，包括在測試時檢索人類研究經驗作為外部技能，以及在研究軌跡上訓練模型以改善對新研究決策的泛化。我們的結果暗示了一條通向AI系統的道路，這些系統不僅從科學的產品中學習，還從發現過程的演變中學習。
